Canada's multiculturalism policy has two key milestones that together answer the query. First, on 8 October 1971, Prime Minister Pierre Elliott Trudeau announced multiculturalism as an official government policy in a statement to the House of Commons, making Canada the first country in the world to introduce such a policy [d6][d4][d5]. Second, the policy was formally enshrined into law when the Canadian Multiculturalism Act received Royal Assent on 21 July 1988, after being introduced on 1 December 1987 by Secretary of State David Crombie [d2][d1][d3]. The 1988 Act provided a legislative framework for the existing 1971 policy, expanding its focus to better reflect Canada's increasingly diverse racial and ethnic composition [d3]. The Act was adopted unanimously by Parliament and was the first national multiculturalism law in the world [d4][d2].
